newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: ANI shareholders remove rebel director.
newsitem.headline: ANI shareholders remove rebel director.

text.p: Shareholders in heavy engineering firm Australian National Industries Ltd on Monday voted to remove Ross Palmer as a director, following a boardroom dispute over the company's handling of its German operations.
Another director, Peter Joseph, who had moved for Palmer's dismissal, was retained on the board in a poll which was collated at the end of the company's six hour annual meeting.
Palmer, the largest personal shareholder in ANI with a stake of five pct, was removed by a vote of 66.08 pct of shareholders to 33.92 pct who supported his re-election.
Joseph, who was the subject of a dismissal motion by Palmer, was retained as a director by a vote of 70.54 pct to 29.46 pct.
Palmer had been on the ANI board for a year and had been critical of the company's handling of its Holter/ABT operations in Germany, which has cost the company more than A$200 million.

Palmer announced last month that he and fellow director Fred Smith had been appointed by other directors to the board to investigate the Holter operations. This statement was issued without the approval of ANI chairman Ted Harris, and was criticised by Peter Joseph as an indication of the board's lack of cohesion.
Smith was narrowly re-elected to the board.
